name: cv-baseline-v4
hypothesis: Era anchor for cv-medium-v4: frozen yamnet linear probe, 400 epochs, on medium now including Hard Negatives.
conclusion: 0.324 (0.262 incl. quiet). Anchor for v4. Not comparable to v3's 0.330: the data changed (Hard Negatives added).

name: v4-ft
hypothesis: Fine-tuning YAMNet layers 12-14 (depth12, backbone LR 1e-5, 30 epochs, linear head) beats the frozen anchor on the new data.
conclusion: +0.051 (0.375). Val sens was still rising at epoch 30, so 30 epochs may understate it. All grid runs use the same 30-epoch budget, so the grid is matched.

name: v4-ft-dense
hypothesis: A Dense(1024) ReLU head on the depth12 fine-tuned trunk beats the linear head.
conclusion: 0.376 vs v4-ft 0.375: no gain from the dense head.

name: v4-ft-ps
hypothesis: Last era's best (fine-tuned depth12 trunk + octave-up pitch-shift twin, linear head) holds up on the Hard Negatives data at 30 epochs.
conclusion: 0.452 (0.372 incl. quiet), +0.128 vs anchor and +0.077 vs v4-ft. Grid winner. Reproduces v3's 0.472/0.454. Hard folds up vs anchor: 1_95 0.07->0.20, 1_150 0.25->0.31, willard 0.39->0.58.

name: v4-ft-ps-dense
hypothesis: A Dense(1024) head on the pitch-shift fine-tuned trunk beats the linear head.
conclusion: 0.432, -0.020 vs v4-ft-ps. The dense head doesn't help; if anything it's slightly worse.

name: v4-ft-ctx
hypothesis: Temporal context (neighbouring frames through a shared depth12 tail) adds to fine-tuning.
conclusion: 0.416, +0.041 vs v4-ft but -0.036 vs v4-ft-ps. Context helps; pitch-shift helps more.

name: v4-ft-ctx-dense
hypothesis: A Dense(1024) head on the context fine-tuned trunk beats the linear head.
conclusion: 0.384, -0.032 vs v4-ft-ctx. The dense head is worse again.

name: v4-ft-psud
hypothesis: Adding an octave-DOWN third view (centre half, resampled) to v4-ft-ps's [plain, up] improves on it.
conclusion: 0.452 (0.371 incl. quiet), +0.000 vs v4-ft-ps. Adding down to up is flat. Down alone and other down methods queued (HANDOFF.md).

name: v4-ft-ps-e60
hypothesis: v4-ft-ps at 60 epochs beats 30 epochs (the epoch confirmation before moderate).
conclusion: 0.468 (0.386 incl. quiet), +0.016 vs v4-ft-ps at 30 epochs. About one delta SD (~0.014), below the ~0.027 MDE. Weak evidence 60 is no worse and may help; 60 is fine for the moderate run.

name: v4-ft-psd
hypothesis: An octave-DOWN second view alone (centre half, resampled), in place of v4-ft-ps's up view, helps over no shift.
conclusion: 0.404 (0.336 incl. quiet), -0.048 vs v4-ft-ps; +0.029 vs v4-ft (0.375), at the ~0.027 MDE. Down alone is at most a small gain; up carries the pitch-shift effect. Hard folds below ps: 1_95 0.167, willard 0.483.

name: v4-ft-pshd
hypothesis: Octave-down resampling applied to both halves (full frame coverage) beats centre-half down.
conclusion: 0.394 (0.323 incl. quiet), -0.058 vs v4-ft-ps; +0.019 vs v4-ft (0.375), noise-level. Both-halves vs centre down: -0.010, no difference. 1_150 0.361 (vs ps 0.312) is a one-fold lead only; 1_95 0.128 lowest of the grid.

name: v4-ft-vd
hypothesis: Octave-down via phase vocoder (duration kept) beats resampled down.
conclusion: 0.401 (0.331 incl. quiet), -0.051 vs v4-ft-ps; +0.026 vs v4-ft (0.375), noise-level. Vocoder vs resample down: -0.003, no difference.

name: v4-ft-vu
hypothesis: Octave-up via phase vocoder (duration kept) beats v4-ft-ps's resampled up.
conclusion: 0.455 (0.377 incl. quiet), +0.003 vs v4-ft-ps. Vocoder up equals resample up; resample stays preferred (no deployment cost measured for the vocoder). Hard folds track ps: 1_95 0.215, 1_150 0.315, willard 0.573.

name: v4-ft-vud
hypothesis: Vocoder up + down views beat a single up view.
conclusion: 0.428 (0.353 incl. quiet), -0.024 vs v4-ft-ps and -0.027 vs v4-ft-vu, at the MDE. Adding down to up does not help; weak sign it hurts with the vocoder. 1_95 0.226 is the grid high at 30 epochs (one fold).

name: v4-ft-pshud
hypothesis: Resampled up + down applied to both halves (four views) beats v4-ft-ps.
conclusion: 0.455 (0.374 incl. quiet), +0.003 vs v4-ft-ps. Flat; not worth 4 views (~2x train time). Ran without RAM kill. 1_150 0.407 is the grid high (one fold, 21 events). Grid verdict: up is the effect, method and down don't matter; v4-ft-ps stays the pick.

name: ps-fast
hypothesis: Reading the octave-up view off the plain STFT and passing it untiled keeps v4-ft-ps's gain at ~1.34x single-view inference cost instead of ~2.27x.
conclusion: 0.432 (0.355 incl. quiet), -0.020 ± 0.014 vs v4-ft-ps, +0.057 vs v4-ft. Seven folds within SD (mean +0.003); 1_114 -0.174 carries the loss. Tiers vs v4-ft-ps: background +0.048, untagged -0.024, loud -0.057 (thin). A speed/accuracy trade, not a drop-in; untested which change (shared STFT vs untiling) costs 1_114.

name: ps-sharedtiled
hypothesis: Shared-STFT up view, tiled. If the shared STFT's coarser frequency resolution is what costs 1_114, this lands near v4-ft-ps-fast on 1_114; if untiling is, it lands near v4-ft-ps.
conclusion: Headline 0.451, flat vs v4-ft-ps (0.452, -0.001+-0.013). 1_114 0.357, down -0.114+-0.037 from v4-ft-ps (0.471); ps-untiled alone loses only -0.078. Shared STFT dominates the 1_114 loss; untiling adds a smaller, roughly independent hit (-0.114 + -0.078 ~= fast's -0.174). Medium's translation changed between comparators and these runs (mech_quadcopter -> mech_machinery, ~46s non-buzz audio, buzz labels unchanged).

name: ps-untiled
hypothesis: v4-ft-ps's resampled up view, untiled. If untiling is what costs 1_114, this lands near v4-ft-ps-fast on 1_114; if the shared STFT is, it lands near v4-ft-ps.
conclusion: Headline 0.439, down -0.013+-0.013 from v4-ft-ps (0.452). 1_114 0.393, down -0.078+-0.037 from v4-ft-ps (0.471); ps-sharedtiled alone loses -0.114, more than untiling alone. Combined with ps-sharedtiled's result the two changes look roughly additive (-0.078 + -0.114 ~= fast's -0.174), not one change or an interaction. Unlike the shared STFT, untiling costs something on the headline even alone. Medium's translation changed between comparators and these runs (mech_quadcopter -> mech_machinery, ~46s non-buzz audio, buzz labels unchanged).

name: ps-gmp
hypothesis: Concatenating global max pool with average pool in the tail preserves transients and lifts the hard folds.
conclusion: Flat (+0.001 ± 0.011). Hard folds 1_95/1_150/1_114 did not improve; 1_37 +0.149 the lone mover. No tier moved (loud +0.011, untagged +0.007, background -0.009).

name: ps-featdrop
hypothesis: Per-view channel dropout on the layer-11 map regularises tail fine-tuning and lifts unseen/hard deployments.
conclusion: Flat headline (+0.009 +/- 0.012); hard folds within noise, background tier slipped. Not worth a repeat.

name: ps-bntrain
hypothesis: Un-freezing tail BatchNorm lets the fine-tuned tail re-normalise for this pool.
conclusion: Best pool-experiment headline so far (+0.027, ~1.9 SD with training noise): suggestive; background tier +0.044, hard folds flat. Repeat seed / combine before adopting; check BN inference behaviour.

name: ps-nosmooth
hypothesis: Removing label smoothing sharpens the negative tail where the 0.5% FPR threshold is read.
conclusion: Headline down (-0.039 +/- 0.015), background tier -0.127, hard folds leaned down; keep label smoothing 0.2.

name: ps-bntrain-repeat
hypothesis: ps-bntrain's +0.027 reproduces on a repeat draw
conclusion: +0.017 (+0.022 two-draw mean): weak confirmation. 1_37 +0.125 reproduces; 1_114 -0.064 and loud -0.039 slip; untagged +0.017, background +0.024. Hard folds 1_95/1_150 not helped.

name: ps-bntrain-e60
hypothesis: Trainable tail BN (+0.027 at 30 ep) compounds with the 60-epoch budget
conclusion: No compounding: -0.011 +/- 0.014 vs v4-ft-ps-e60; the 30-epoch gain looks like faster convergence absorbed by longer training. Hard folds flat; 1_29 and 1_114 drop. Not adopted at 60 epochs.

name: ps-bntrain-featdrop
hypothesis: Channel dropout of the layer-11 map compounds with trainable tail BatchNorm (BN adapts statistics, dropout regularises site-specific channels)
conclusion: 0.448 vs 0.452 control (-0.004 +/- 0.014), below BN alone (0.479/0.469): dropout erases the BN gain; no compounding

name: ps-bntrain-gmp
hypothesis: With trainable tail BN the max-pooled transient channel may become usable (ps-gmp alone was neutral)
conclusion: No gain: 0.447 vs 0.452, below ps-bntrain 0.479 and repeat 0.469; GMP does not compound with BN training

name: ps-depth10
hypothesis: Two more trainable blocks in the tail let it re-form features for this pool and lift hard folds
conclusion: Weak headline gain (+0.021 +/- 0.013); 1_37 up, 1_95/1_150 flat, 1_114 -0.065; tiers all leaned up slightly. Hard folds not helped; same signature as ps-bntrain.

name: ps-cutout
hypothesis: Masking one time row or frequency column of the layer-11 map per view regularises spatial structure and helps deployments with different buzz placement
conclusion: Null: flat mean, hard fold 1_95 slightly worse, background tier down; spatial cutout does not help

name: ps-bntrain-depth10
hypothesis: Deeper tail has more BN layers with mismatched AudioSet stats; adapting them may add to depth-10 gain
conclusion: Null: BN training erases depth-10 gain (0.455 vs 0.473); two folds collapse, keep frozen BN

name: ps-noise
hypothesis: Unstructured Gaussian noise on the layer-11 map regularises the tail against deployment shift without removing cues
conclusion: Null: +0.009 within noise; background tier -0.076 like cutout

name: ps-ema
hypothesis: Averaging the late weight trajectory reduces training noise in the fine-tuned tail without changing budget or data
conclusion: Null: -0.008 +/- 0.012. Background tier -0.076, loud -0.032, untagged flat; 1_29 and 1_114 down (~2 SD), 1_37/1_150 up, 1_95 flat. EMA does not help.

name: ps-untied
hypothesis: Views have different statistics; per-view tails let each specialise vs the shared TimeDistributed tail
conclusion: Null: +0.006 +/- 0.012. Background tier -0.047, untagged +0.014, loud +0.011, quiet +0.017; 1_29 down (~2 SD), 1_37 up, 1_95 flat. Shared tail is not the bottleneck.

name: ps-depth10-repeat
hypothesis: ps-depth10's +0.021 is real, not training noise
conclusion: Reproduces: +0.035 (draws +0.021/+0.035, mean +0.028). Background +0.050, untagged +0.034, loud -0.017. 1_37/1_29 up both draws, 1_114 down both, 1_150 flat/down, 1_95 weakly up. Modest real lever; hard folds 1_150/1_114 not helped.

name: ps-depth8
hypothesis: Cutting trainable tail two blocks earlier (layer 7) extends the depth10 gain; ladder 12->10->8 tests saturation
conclusion: Gain grows monotonically with trainable depth (0.452 -> 0.480 -> 0.515) via background/untagged tiers, loud tier -0.048; single draw, repeat and try depth 6 next

name: ps-depth8-repeat
hypothesis: ps-depth8's +0.063 is a single draw; repeat it before building on the depth ladder.
conclusion: Confirmed: +0.057 (draws +0.063/+0.057, mean 0.512), +0.032 over depth10's two-draw mean. Untagged +0.057, background +0.040, loud -0.024 (122 frames). 1_37 up both draws; 1_95/1_150 lean up both draws within SD. Next: depth 6.

name: ps-depth6
hypothesis: Cutting the trainable tail two blocks earlier than depth8 (layer 5) extends the 12->10->8 ladder
conclusion: Ladder probably peaks at depth8: depth6 gives back half the gain (-0.031 +/- 0.015 vs depth8-repeat), losses on hard folds 1_114 (-0.128 +/- 0.035) and 1_150 (-0.102 +/- 0.044); tiers vs depth8: untagged/background down, loud/quiet slightly up. Possibly overfit at same LR/epochs (untested). See notes.md.

name: ps-depth4
hypothesis: Cutting the trainable tail at layer 3 (layers 4-14) extends the 12->10->8->6 ladder
conclusion: Ties depth8 (+0.011 vs two-draw mean, within ~0.015) at ~2x compute; depth ladder saturated at 8, depth6's 0.478 likely an odd draw. vs depth8-repeat: 1_150 -0.10 +/- 0.04, 1_95 +0.07, 1_114 +0.07; background tier +0.04. No repeat.

name: site-adv-w01
hypothesis: Folds are deployments, so a head predicting the training fold behind a gradient-reversal layer should push the fine-tuned tail to drop site identity and lift the hard folds; dose ladder on the reversal weight (0.1 / 0.3 / 1.0).
conclusion: Weight 0.1: 0.225 vs 0.515/0.509 (ladder 0.1/0.3/1.0 = 0.225/0.132/0.126); every fold and every tier (loud, untagged, background) down by many SDs, hard folds included. Not a test of site invariance: the reversed gradient maximises an unbounded site cross-entropy, train loss runs to ~15x chance and held-out class loss spikes to 1e2-1e6 mid-run, while the adversary still names the fold at 4-8x chance at epoch 30. Plain gradient reversal is unstable in this recipe from 0.1 up; see site-conf-w01 for the bounded form.

name: site-adv-w03
hypothesis: Folds are deployments, so a head predicting the training fold behind a gradient-reversal layer should push the fine-tuned tail to drop site identity and lift the hard folds; dose ladder on the reversal weight (0.1 / 0.3 / 1.0).
conclusion: Weight 0.3: 0.132 vs 0.515/0.509 (ladder 0.1/0.3/1.0 = 0.225/0.132/0.126); every fold and every tier (loud, untagged, background) down by many SDs, hard folds included. Not a test of site invariance: the reversed gradient maximises an unbounded site cross-entropy, train loss runs to ~15x chance and held-out class loss spikes to 1e2-1e6 mid-run, while the adversary still names the fold at 4-8x chance at epoch 30. Plain gradient reversal is unstable in this recipe from 0.1 up; see site-conf-w01 for the bounded form.

name: site-adv-w10
hypothesis: Folds are deployments, so a head predicting the training fold behind a gradient-reversal layer should push the fine-tuned tail to drop site identity and lift the hard folds; dose ladder on the reversal weight (0.1 / 0.3 / 1.0).
conclusion: Weight 1.0: 0.126 vs 0.515/0.509 (ladder 0.1/0.3/1.0 = 0.225/0.132/0.126); every fold and every tier (loud, untagged, background) down by many SDs, hard folds included. Not a test of site invariance: the reversed gradient maximises an unbounded site cross-entropy, train loss runs to ~15x chance and held-out class loss spikes to 1e2-1e6 mid-run, while the adversary still names the fold at 4-8x chance at epoch 30. Plain gradient reversal is unstable in this recipe from 0.1 up; see site-conf-w01 for the bounded form.

name: site-conf-w01
hypothesis: The site-adv ladder diverged because gradient reversal maximises an unbounded cross-entropy; pushing a stop-gradient site head's prediction toward uniform (KL, bounded below) should keep training stable, drive the adversary toward chance and lift the hard folds.
conclusion: Uninformative about site invariance. Training is stable (val_loss 0.62-0.84, no spikes) but the tail flattens the pooled code: held-out ins_buzz logit SD 0.08-0.20 vs the control's 0.65-1.20, per-epoch sensitivity never above 0.10 in any fold (control 0.2-0.6) and 0.000-0.016 at epoch 30; all tiers at chance (loud 0.819 -> 0.021, untagged 0.531 -> 0.006, background 0.444 -> 0.001). The adversary still names the training fold at 7-9x chance, so class signal went before site signal. val_loss cannot detect this: a near-constant output sits in the trained model's basin. Remaining forms (non-buzz frames only; bounded-above entropy term with a ramp) are IDEAS.md item 30.

name: site-neg-w01
hypothesis: site-conf-w01 flattened the pooled code because site and label are dependent in the pool (Hard Negatives folds hold no buzz); applying the KL-to-uniform site term to non-buzz training frames only should keep the class output alive and let site invariance be tested.
conclusion: ONE FOLD ONLY: the built-in gate (fold-1 sens < 0.3 at epoch 10) stopped the CV after 1_29, so metrics here are that fold, not a headline. 1_29 0.001 vs 0.568 (-0.567 +/- 0.081); its untagged, background and loud tiers all at chance; buzz logit SD 0.09 vs 1.20. Non-buzz scope collapses the class output exactly like site-conf-w01, so the site/label dependence is not the sole cause. Plumbing control (same site head, tail term off, test_site_w0): 1_29 0.639, and the unopposed site head reaches 84% training-fold accuracy (chance 2.1%); under the term it sits at 18% with the class signal gone. Remaining lead: a bounded, ramped term (item 30b).

name: site-ent-ramp
hypothesis: The KL site term collapsed the class output because it is unbounded above and hit an untrained head at full weight; the site head's negative entropy (bounded by ln 48), ramped from 0 to 0.1 over 10 epochs, should let the class head survive so site invariance can be tested.
conclusion: ONE FOLD ONLY: the built-in gate stopped the CV after 1_29, so metrics here are that fold, not a headline. 1_29 0.000 vs 0.568 (-0.568 +/- 0.082); untagged, background and loud tiers of that fold at chance; buzz logit SD 0.08 vs 1.20. Per-epoch: sensitivity tracks the weight-zero control through epoch 3 (0.52 at weight 0.02), breaks at weight 0.03-0.05 and is at chance from 0.06, while the site head is still at 0.33-0.38 accuracy (15x chance; 0.84 unopposed). Third shape of the term with the same outcome: class signal goes before site identity does. Family moved to IDEAS.md Ruled out.

name: pseudo-label
hypothesis: Confident pseudo-labels from unlabelled audio of the training deployments widen the negative tail where the 0.5% FPR threshold is read, so a student beats its own teacher on untagged/loud and on 1_95, 1_114, 1_37; falsified if the student is within the headline SD of the teacher
conclusion: Null: student 0.475 vs its teacher 0.466 (+0.009 +- 0.014). Tiers: loud +0.025 (122 frames), untagged +0.007, background -0.028, none outside noise; 1_37 +0.074 +- 0.035 is the only fold near 2 SD, 1_95 flat. Confident frames are ones the teacher already gets right. Caveat: the teacher, meant as a third ps-depth8 draw, scored 0.466 against 0.515/0.509 (-0.043 +- 0.015 vs ps-depth8-repeat), unexplained; do not read the student against 0.509. Untested: held-out fold's own unlabelled audio (Luke's call), a larger pool, the dropped mid-confidence band. notes.md on exp/pseudo-label

name: ps-depth8-redraw
hypothesis: pseudo-label's stage-1 teacher scored 0.466 where two ps-depth8 draws scored 0.515 and 0.509; if nothing in 03_train or medium drifted since 2026-10-01, a plain ps-depth8 CV from current main lands with the earlier draws, and the 0.466 belongs to the PSEUDO_SET path or to noise
conclusion: No drift: 0.497, within noise of both earlier draws (three-draw mean 0.507, spread 0.009). pseudo-label_teacher is 0.031 +- 0.015 below this draw, so the PSEUDO_SET path may not be the plain recipe (unresolved, one sample). Tiers flat (untagged -0.007; background -0.038 follows 1_29; loud +0.037 on 122 frames). Fold scatter between identical fine-tuned runs reaches ~0.1 (1_114 -0.098, 1_29 -0.082, 1_95 +0.048): single-run fold deltas on this recipe need a repeat. ps-depth8-r3 is the fresh control for ps-d8-taps and ps-d8-foldbal

name: ps-d8-taps
hypothesis: The ps-depth8 readout sees only layer 14's pooled map; the hard folds fail on confusers (jet, trill) that mid-level time-frequency texture may separate, so letting the class Dense also read GAP of layers 10 and 12 inside the trainable tail should lift untagged/loud and 1_95, 1_114, 1_37
conclusion: Null, leaning negative: -0.016 +- 0.012 vs ps-depth8-r3, and below all three plain draws (0.497, 0.509, 0.515). The predicted folds did not rise: 1_95 -0.062 +- 0.022, 1_150 -0.083 +- 0.052 (each unsure, since identical runs scatter up to ~0.1 per fold), 1_114 -0.022, 1_37 +0.024 within SD. Tiers opposite to the prediction: untagged -0.025, loud -0.036, background +0.034 (53 +0.036). Untried: taps below the trainable tail (layers 7-9), or a non-linear readout over them

name: ps-d8-foldbal
hypothesis: The loss is a frame mean but the headline a deployment mean, and deployments differ ~100x in frames; weighting each training frame by its fold's n_frames^-0.5 (group-balanced ERM, p=0.5) should lift held-out deployments, the hard folds most.
conclusion: Negative: -0.041 +- 0.015 vs ps-depth8-r3 (-0.053 +- 0.016 vs ps-depth8-repeat). Only 1_114 moved beyond its SD (-0.125 +- 0.053); 1_37, 1_150, 1_29, 53 down within ~1 SD, none up. Tiers all down: loud -0.036, untagged -0.044, background -0.032. Down-weighting big deployments costs more than up-weighting small ones buys; one draw at p=0.5.

name: ps-d8-aves
hypothesis: AVES features, a repeated +0.02 to +0.04 on frozen YAMNet probes in closed eras, still add information once the YAMNet tail is fine-tuned: headline above ps-depth8-r3 by more than ~0.014 with untagged/loud up
conclusion: Null: the frozen-probe AVES gain does not carry over to a fine-tuned tail. Not neutral per fold: 1_29 up (background +0.097), 1_114 down for the second era running, loud -0.037, untagged -0.010; single draw. Offline check on the AVES columns alone: the head's regime reads them (0.217; converged standardized ridge 0.280), so not a readout artifact, but the joint head's AVES share was not measured. AVES2/BEATs (IDEAS item 29) not run: same question, ~1.5x faster encoder, still under the injunction. Details in exp/ps-d8-aves notes.md.

name: ps-d8-ensemble
hypothesis: Draws of one recipe scatter because each fold's threshold rests on ~30 negatives that the draws score differently; the mean of three draws' ins_buzz logits should beat the best single draw (0.515), more than +0.02 over the members' mean
conclusion: Positive: 3-draw mean 0.558 (0.467 incl. quiet) vs members 0.515/0.509/0.497, +0.049 +- 0.011 over the median draw and above the best member on 7 of 8 folds; pairs +0.035 to +0.044, a disjoint depth4+depth10 pair replicates (0.559), five mixed-depth members 0.575 (not flat yet). Thresholds fall ~0.2 logits on every fold (negatives correlate 0.62 between draws, buzz 0.88). Hard folds up: 1_95 +0.076 +- 0.022, 1_150 +0.090 +- 0.041; 1_114 unsure. Tiers: untagged +0.049, background +0.063, loud +0.042 (122 frames). Costs N trainings; no new representation. Follow-ups in IDEAS 30 (member count, K tails on the shared stem) and D1 (ensemble teacher for the lite tier). notes.md has every member table.

name: ps-d8-ens-same5
hypothesis: The ensemble gain keeps growing with members of one recipe: a five-draw same-recipe ps-depth8 mean lands above the three-draw mean (0.558) and within 0.02 of the mixed-depth five (0.575), so member count, not depth diversity, is what the mixed five bought. Falsified if it stays at the three's level.
conclusion: Falsified as written: same-recipe five 0.558 = the three (+0.000 +- 0.006; ens3 was the best of the ten 3-subsets, which average 0.545, fours 0.553). Returns past three members are within the eval SD. Depth diversity is not shown either: ensemble lift over the member mean is +0.066 same-recipe, +0.069 mixed, so the mixed five led because r4/r5 drew weak (five draws span 0.464-0.515, SD 0.022; single-draw trunk deltas under ~0.03 need a repeat). Tiers vs ens3: background +0.012, rest within 0.006; no fold moves 2 SD; 1_114 is -0.087 +- 0.025 against the mixed five; 1_95 stays 0.309 at any member count. Still +0.061 +- 0.011 over a single draw, all folds up.

name: ps-d8-ktails
hypothesis: K=3 independent tails on the shared stem, trained in one job on identical batches, decorrelate from the head init alone, so their logit mean lands within 0.02 of the same-recipe threes (mean 0.545) with member correlations near the separate draws' (0.62 negatives, 0.88 buzz); falsified if the mean lands at a single draw's level with members correlating well above that
conclusion: Mixed. Decorrelation needs no independent data order: tails correlate 0.61 / 0.87 and the mean takes the full ensemble step (+0.056 over members). But the headline is 0.524, under ens3 (-0.034 +- 0.010) and all ten same-recipe threes, because all three members sit at the bottom of the single-draw range (0.466-0.470 vs mean 0.492, spread 0.004): a shared order gives one draw of the member level, not three. Against the median single draw +0.027 +- 0.012 (background +0.051, untagged +0.028, loud -0.036); 1_150 and 1_95 do not get the lift separate draws gave them (-0.081 +- 0.039, -0.048 +- 0.021 vs ens3), 1_29 -0.091 +- 0.023. No time saved (46 min/fold vs 3 x 16). For an ensemble teacher, train members as separate runs.

name: ens3-moderate
hypothesis: On moderate the 3-draw logit mean of the teacher's recipe scores more than +0.02 over its members' mean, with thresholds lower on every fold; falsifier: within 0.02 (draws rank negatives alike on 5x the data)
conclusion: Held: +0.037 over the members' mean, +0.028 +- 0.006 over the best draw (the teacher), smaller than medium's +0.049 but clear of 0.02; every fold above its members' mean (1_29 +0.058, 1_37 +0.055, 53 +0.031, 1_11 +0.024, 1_143 +0.019; only 1_143 against draw 1 is flat, -0.005 +- 0.010); tiers: background +0.054, untagged +0.035, loud +0.013, quiet +0.014; two draws give +0.026 to +0.031, the third ~+0.008; draw spread 0.018. Baseline here is draw 1, not the members' mean. Untested through a student (IDEAS D1).

name: ps2-depth8
hypothesis: A two-octave-up view moves the buzz fundamental further into well-resolved mel bands and adds sensitivity beyond the one-octave pitchshift; predicted > +0.03 over ps-depth8-r3 and above the 0.507 three-draw mean, untagged up
conclusion: Falsified: below every ps-depth8 draw, untagged down, losses on the target hard folds and biggest at 1_114 (tile-seam fold); the 4x tile / 0.24 s window likely costs more than the second octave adds. Only a seam-free two-octave view remains untested.

name: ps-depth8-e60
hypothesis: Depth8 fine-tunes more blocks than depth12 (where 60 epochs gave +0.016), so a 60-epoch budget lifts the headline >0.03 over ps-depth8-r3; falsified if within ~0.02 of the three-draw mean or below it (overfit).
conclusion: Falsified, overfit side: -0.060 +- 0.015, below all five plain depth8 draws. Tiers: loud -0.076, untagged -0.063, background -0.013: isolated detections lose. Hard folds lose most. Held-out val_loss per fold bottoms at epochs 2-19 (median ~9) in both 30- and 60-epoch runs and rises 30->60 on 7/8 folds. Keep depth8 at <=30 epochs for moderate; below 30 tested by ps-depth8-e15.

name: ps-depth8-e15
hypothesis: Depth8's held-out val_loss bottoms at epochs 2-19 and e60 overfit, so a 15-epoch budget nearer the loss minimum lifts the headline >=0.02 over the three-draw mean (0.507); falsified if within ~0.02 or below (undertrained).
conclusion: Falsified, undertrained side: -0.039 +- 0.013, all on hard folds and 1_37; tiers untagged -0.041, loud -0.045, background +0.002 (drones already fitted). Ladder 15/30/60 = 0.458/0.497-0.515/0.437: 30 is the depth8 optimum. val_loss is lower at 15 than 30 on 7/8 folds, so it does not track sens@fpr here; _consensus_epoch (pooled val_loss) would pick ~9 and undertrain a depth8 shipped/moderate model; set the budget explicitly. Surfaced to Luke in notes.md.

name: lp-ft
hypothesis: Warm-starting the head for 10 epochs (tail frozen) before the depth8 fine-tune reduces feature distortion and lifts the headline >= 0.02 over the depth8 three-draw mean 0.507, on untagged and the hard folds.
conclusion: Negative: -0.058 +- 0.013 vs matched r3, loss in untagged (-0.062; loud/background/quiet flat) and on hard folds 1_114 (-0.204) and 1_150 (-0.139). Budget confound (10 extra head-only epochs) noted; head warm-start is not a depth8 lever.

name: pauc-l03
hypothesis: A one-way pAUC term ranking ins_buzz positives above the batch's top-5% negatives (lambda 0.3) lifts the headline >= 0.02 over the depth8 three-draw mean 0.507, mostly on confuser-thresholded folds (1_95, 1_114, 1_37).
conclusion: Falsified: -0.091 +- 0.015 vs ps-depth8-r3; target folds lost most (1_114 -0.170, 1_150 -0.139, 1_95 -0.121); buzz logit SD 0.8-1.5, not a collapse. Tiers: background -0.100, untagged -0.091, loud -0.039, quiet flat. IDEAS #33 trimmed to the lambda 0.1 rung.

name: mixstyle-dep
hypothesis: Within-fold MixStyle on the cached layer-7 map perturbs deployment style while keeping content, lifting the headline >= 0.02 over the three-draw depth8 mean (0.507) on untagged/loud and on 1_95 / 1_114.
conclusion: Falsified: -0.031 +- 0.014 vs matched control (-0.041 vs three-draw mean), losses on targeted hard folds 1_95 (-0.045 +- 0.021) and 1_150 (-0.074 +- 0.044) and on loud/untagged; only background gained (+0.038). No logit collapse (buzz SD 0.59-1.10). The cross-training-fold variant is untested and stays as IDEAS #31.

name: llrd-depth4
hypothesis: Layer-wise LR decay (0.7 per block) on the depth4 tail keeps lower blocks near AudioSet features and lifts the headline >= 0.02 over ps-depth4 (0.523) and the depth8 three-draw mean (0.507), making depth past 8 usable
conclusion: Falsified: -0.058 +- 0.016 vs ps-depth4, -0.042 vs depth8 mean. Freezing-ish the lower blocks hurts; their adaptation was helping, not overfitting. Losses on 1_114, 1_95, 1_143, 1_11; untagged -0.055, background -0.058, loud +0.053 (122 frames), quiet -0.020. Logit SDs 0.57-1.22, no collapse. Milder decay or LLRD on depth8 untested and not encouraged.

name: mixstyle-xfold
hypothesis: MixStyle with partners drawn across deployments (the rotation's other training folds) mixes the recorder/site style that actually differs between deployments and lifts the headline >= 0.02 over the depth8 three-draw mean (0.507), with 1_95/1_114/1_150 up
conclusion: Falsified: -0.061 +- 0.015 vs ps-depth8-r3, -0.071 vs three-draw mean, and -0.030 +- 0.013 below within-fold mixstyle-dep. 1_114 collapses (-0.292 +- 0.066, -0.255 vs mixstyle-dep), 1_150 -0.092, 1_95 -0.045; untagged -0.070, loud -0.030, background +0.017. Logit SDs 0.51-1.16, no collapse. Layer-7 channel statistics carry content, not just style; the MixStyle line on this map is closed.

name: ps-d8-soup
hypothesis: The uniform weight soup of three depth8 draws, which share the pretrained YAMNet tail init, scores at or above its best member and closes most of the gap to their logit ensemble; WiSE-FT toward the pretrained tail tests over-adaptation.
conclusion: Falsified: soup -0.071 +- 0.019 below best member m1 and -0.121 +- 0.022 below the 3-member logit ensemble; 53 -0.186 +- 0.096, 1_150 -0.148 +- 0.068, 1_29 -0.143 +- 0.041, 1_95 -0.045 +- 0.023, 1_114 +0.080 +- 0.034; logits shrink ~2.5x, so the draws left a shared basin (random-init heads). soup.py parity on m1 alone exact (0 flips). WiSE loses monotonically with A: tail fine-tuning is signal. Tiers vs m1: loud -0.007; see notes. Side: ensemble 0.531 (+0.034 +- 0.014 vs ps-depth8-r3) repeats ps-d8-ensemble; members 0.481/0.470/0.472, six-draw depth8 mean 0.491.

name: bn-pooled
hypothesis: Re-estimating the frozen-BN depth8 tail's moving statistics on the rotation's own training folds (no labels, no weight change) aligns normalisation with this data's domain and gains >= +0.02 on the same weights.
conclusion: Falsified: AdaBN collapses ranking on every fold (1_11 -0.596 +- 0.102, 1_29 -0.536 +- 0.074, 1_150 -0.361 +- 0.066, 1_95 -0.233 +- 0.038; all folds <= 0.073) though logits still spread (SD 0.08-4.4); tiers loud -0.792, untagged -0.476, background -0.427, quiet -0.101. Mean shifts small (<= 0.052). Weights co-adapted to frozen AudioSet stats; post-hoc swap misaligns them (contrast ps-bntrain, stats moved during training). Parity of soup.py path exact. IDEAS #37 (b)/(c) inherit the problem on frozen-BN fine-tunes.

name: pauc-l01
hypothesis: At lambda 0.1 the pAUC term's loss at 0.3 was a dose overshoot: the headline lands at or above the depth8 three-draw mean 0.507 with hard folds up.
conclusion: Falsified: 0.426, between the control (0.497) and lambda 0.3 (0.406), so the decline is monotone in dose, meeting the idea's falsifier; low-FPR-loss family closed (with pairwise-rank, tail-loss, mech-margin). Largest losses on hard folds 1_114 -0.235, 1_150 -0.139. No logit collapse (buzz SD 0.87-1.37). Tiers: untagged -0.071, background -0.043, loud -0.012, quiet -0.010.

name: eq-aug-d8
hypothesis: Random recorder-response (EQ) augmentation makes the depth8 tail rely less on a recorder's spectral colouring and lifts held-out deployments by >= +0.02, with untagged or loud up.
conclusion: Falsified: -0.008 +- 0.015, inside the ~0.014 training-noise floor, and no loudness tier moved beyond noise (background +0.014, quiet +0.016). Both hard Diel Drivers folds fell (1_150 -0.120 +- 0.044, 1_95 -0.062 +- 0.028) while 1_143 rose +0.054 +- 0.041, with no recorder pattern. Recorder colouring is not what limits depth8 on held-out deployments; buzz logit SD healthy (0.51-1.21).

name: snr-aug-d8
hypothesis: SNR-relative noise augmentation, unhelpful on the frozen probe, lifts held-out deployments by >= +0.02 once the depth8 tail has capacity to use it, with untagged/quiet and 1_150 up.
conclusion: Falsified and harmful: -0.063 +- 0.014, ~4.5x the noise floor. Loss is in untagged (-0.067) and on the hard folds: 1_114 -0.312 +- 0.050, 1_150 -0.120 +- 0.045, 1_95 -0.051 +- 0.031; easy folds within noise. Buzz logit SD healthy (0.58-1.26). Noise augmentation closed at the trunk as on the probe.

name: gain-aug-d8
hypothesis: Random ±10 dB gain copies teach the depth8 tail level invariance and lift held-out deployments by >= +0.02, with untagged, quiet and 1_150 up.
conclusion: Falsified: -0.013 +- 0.014, inside the noise floor. quiet (+0.027) and background (+0.030) tiers moved the predicted way, weakly (one draw; quiet is outside the headline); untagged -0.016. Hard folds fell (1_150 -0.055 +- 0.037, 1_95 -0.041 +- 0.029, 1_114 -0.046 +- 0.030), like eq and snr. Buzz logit SD healthy (0.55-1.21).

name: pitch-aug-d8
hypothesis: Random ±2-semitone pitch-shift copies widen the buzz fundamentals the depth8 tail sees and lift held-out deployments by >= +0.02, with untagged and a hard fold (1_95/1_150/1_114) up.
conclusion: Falsified and harmful: -0.046 +- 0.014. The flagged 1_114 risk came true (-0.207 +- 0.047); 1_150 -0.132 +- 0.044, 1_95 -0.073 +- 0.032; 1_29 +0.093 +- 0.040. untagged -0.052, background +0.046. Batch 40 together: eq -0.008, gain -0.013, pitch -0.046, snr -0.063; all took 1_150 down, none lifted a hard fold. Buzz logit SD healthy (0.53-1.26).

name: binary-d8
hypothesis: With a fine-tuned depth8 tail, collapsing the 14 non-buzz classes into one nonbuzz target frees capacity for the buzz boundary (headline >= +0.02, untagged up), or else removes the confuser supervision that keeps 1_114/1_95 negatives down (hard folds fall).
conclusion: Falsified, mechanism (b): -0.116 +- 0.019 (null on a frozen probe, binary-control). Hard folds fell most (1_150 -0.185, 1_95 -0.166, 1_114 -0.158), background tier -0.166, untagged -0.107; only willard rose (+0.044 +- 0.023, weak). With a trainable trunk the named non-buzz classes carry features the buzz boundary needs; keep the full class set for fine-tuned recipes. Note (2026-10-21): binary peaks at epoch 4 (control ~27), so epoch 30 overstates the loss; at the cross-fold epoch (tools/epoch_rule_audit.py) it is 0.386 vs 0.412 incl. quiet (-0.026), still worse, mostly 1_95 and 1_150. Direction stands, size does not.

name: plain-d8
hypothesis: (1) At depth8 the octave-up view still carries a real share: plain depth8 lands >= 0.03 below ps-depth8-r3. (2) A plain-view member decorrelates an ensemble better than a same-recipe draw: plain-d8 + two ps-depth8 draws >= ps-d8-ens3 (0.558) + 0.02.
conclusion: (1) Confirmed: -0.079 +- 0.014, mostly the trill fold 1_114 (-0.345 +- 0.048; other seven mean -0.041); untagged -0.083, loud -0.052, background -0.015. (2) Falsified: swapping plain-d8 for any ps draw gives 0.526-0.534 vs ens3 0.558, and adding it to a ps pair lowers the pair (-0.006 to -0.022); 1_114 drags the mean, weak 1_150 gain only. Ensemble members must be individually strong; tables in exp/plain-d8 notes.md.

name: sam-d8
hypothesis: Sharpness-aware minimization seeks flat minima, the best-supported single predictor of domain generalization; each held-out fold is an unseen deployment, so SAM should lift the headline >= +0.02 over ps-depth8-r3
conclusion: Falsified: -0.005 ± 0.013. Hard folds 1_95 -0.037 ± 0.021 and 1_150 -0.055 ± 0.044 leaned down, 1_114 +0.044 ± 0.049 unsure; 53 +0.060 ± 0.025. Tiers: background +0.058, loud -0.052 (thin), untagged -0.010. Flatness proxies (EMA, soup, now SAM) don't help here; ~3x compute.

name: ps2-seamfree-d8
hypothesis: A seam-free two-octave-up view (3.84 s of real centred audio resampled 4:1, no tiling) fixes the tiled ps2-depth8's 1_114 loss and lifts the headline >= +0.02 over ps-depth8-r3 and above the 0.507 three-draw mean
conclusion: Headline flat (+0.012 ± 0.017; +0.029 ± 0.018 vs tiled ps2-depth8). One large hard-fold gain: 1_114 0.670 (+0.256 ± 0.069), above every earlier depth8 run (max 0.512); weak losses on 1_150 (-0.092 ± 0.057) and 1_95 (-0.037 ± 0.031). Removing the seams fixed the tiled view's 1_114 loss. Not falsified (at the three-draw mean); a large gain, so one repeat draw should check 1_114 and 1_150. Tiers: untagged +0.015, loud +0.020, background -0.026.

name: pitch-aux-d8
hypothesis: Supervising within-buzz pitch structure (as binary-d8 showed non-buzz classes shape trunk features) sharpens the buzz boundary: headline >= +0.02 with untagged or a hard fold up
conclusion: Null (-0.004 ± 0.013). untagged flat, loud -0.036 (122 frames, unsure), quiet +0.015. Hard folds fell: 1_150 -0.088 ± 0.045, 1_95 -0.051 ± 0.028; 1_37/1_11/1_114 up within ~1-2 SD. Aux outputs at inverse-frequency weight (~3x ins_buzz's combined); a lighter aux weight and the frozen-probe arm are untested. Not worth a repeat.

name: noquiet-d8
hypothesis: Dropping quiet/faint buzz samples from training sharpens the boundary for audible buzz: headline >= +0.02 with untagged or loud up
conclusion: Hurts: -0.037 ± 0.013, untagged -0.048, hard folds 1_150/1_95/1_114 each about -0.10 to -0.13. Quiet buzz is useful positive training signal; the standing rule stands.
